To compute the availability of the end-to-end request path, we need to calculate the probability that all four services are available. Since each service is independently available 99.9 percent of the time, we can multiply their individual availability probabilities together.

Availability of each service = 99.9% = 0.999
Availability of all four services = 0.999 × 0.999 × 0.999 × 0.999 = 0.9999

So, the availability of the end-to-end request path is approximately 99.99%.

To compute the approximate monthly unavailable time, we can calculate the probability that at least one service is unavailable. This is equivalent to 1 minus the probability that all services are available.

Probability that all services are available = 0.9999
Probability that at least one service is unavailable = 1 - 0.9999 = 0.0001

Since there are 30 days in a month, the approximate monthly unavailable time is:

Unavailable time = 0.0001 × 30 days ≈ 0.003 days

Therefore, the request path is approximately 99.99% available, and it is unavailable for about 0.003 days (or approximately 1 hour and 24 minutes) per month.
